components.explanation: We now analyze the case of the perfect algorithm (PA) which fully observes and filters based on both message quality and sender distance.
searchPhrases: solution algorithm in innovation, analytics, and technology

conditions: We now analyze the case of the perfect algorithm (PA) which fully observes and filters based on both message quality and sender distance.

The intuition is fairly straightforward: given that the platform can perfectly observe the utility that the receiver will get, it filters out all content that would decrease the receiver’s total payoff.

components.explanation: As the quality algorithm filters out any message with quality less than t∗, senders can increase their base quality qj to make sure their items are not being filtered by the platform.

conditions: Examining the profit function and its first and second order conditions, the profit is locally maximized only when qj ≥t∗.

Using the result from Section 4, suppose the platform sets t∗= c + φ as the threshold for filtering quality, then the probability that an item from any senders passes filtering is Pr(Q > t∗) = min(q + 1 −t∗, 1).
